summary: The change adds a new LoyaltyTier model/table that neither the old nor new Saleor version interacts with regarding customer notes. deploy_new runs the new version's Django migration (which creates account_loyaltytier) then starts the new version. Both versions continue serving concurrently; the old version ignores the new table, and the note column on account_user is known to both, so write consistency is maintained. After retire_old, only the new version remains.
write_consistency: Both versions include the 'note' column in their Django save() operations; the old version's save() only writes known columns, so 'note' is always written explicitly. The new version's migration creates the new LoyaltyTier table without altering account_user or the note column. Concurrent writes to 'note' from both versions remain consistent, with the most recently written value prevailing, matching the runner's cross-version check.

stages.description: Retire the old Saleor version, ending its traffic against the database.
